record.original_question: Let M be a closed surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Is it true that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M eventually enters the subset where the curvature is strictly negative?

evidence.quote: Let M be a surface of genus 2 with a Riemannian metric of nonpositive curvature. Show that, with probability 1, a random geodesic in M runs into the set of negative curvature.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $M$ be a closed orientable surface of genus $2$ equipped with a smooth Riemannian metric of nonpositive Gaussian curvature, and let $N\subset M$ denote the open subset of points at which the curvature is strictly negative. Consider the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle $T^1 M$ together with its Liouville (normalized) measure $\mu$, which is invariant under the flow. Call a unit tangent vector $v\in T^1 M$ "random" if it is generic with respect to $\mu$. Prove or disprove: for $\mu$-almost every $v\in T^1 M$, the geodesic $\gamma_v\colon\mathbb{R}\to M$ with initial vector $v$ satisfies $\gamma_v(t)\in N$ for some $t\in\mathbb{R}$ (equivalently, the geodesic eventually enters the region of strictly negative curvature).
artifact.category_tag: Geodesic flows on nonpositively curved surfaces
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a well-known problem in the open problem list on geodesics maintained by Burns and Matveev. Related results establish ergodicity of the geodesic flow on the set of vectors whose geodesics meet the negative-curvature region (under finiteness assumptions on flat components), but a complete unconditional resolution for arbitrary nonpositively curved metrics on a genus-2 surface does not appear to be documented. Status appears to remain open/unverified.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Questions About Geodesics (Burns–Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Problem list including questions on nonpositively curved surfaces and the behavior of generic geodesics relative to flat regions.
status_evidence.claim: The problem appears in a curated list of open problems about geodesics.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of geodesic flows on surfaces of nonpositive curvature
status_evidence.snippet: Ergodicity of the geodesic flow on a nonpositively curved surface of genus ≥ 2 is proved under the condition that the negative-curvature set has finitely many connected components.
status_evidence.claim: Related ergodicity results exist but require additional hypotheses, suggesting the unconditional question remains unsettled.
